title: A Sea of Empires
scope: All 31 present-day places in rough.tsv, expanded to 36 historical tracks. This is a scoped regional chronology, not an inventory of every Caribbean cay or mainland state.
baseline: 1450 is a graphical starting point, not an origin date. Indigenous history reaches back millennia. Initial states are schematic regional context, not claims that a single people continuously governed a modern territory.
method: Track effective external administration and separately recorded sovereign title. Claims and geographically limited raids are annotations. A control change marks the principal colonial administration, not uniform control of every community. Years and circa dates retain their stated precision.
sovereignty: Sovereign-title view records the framework used by colonial governments and later states, not a judgment that conquest lawfully extinguished Indigenous sovereignty. Disputed and shared situations use a distinct lane. The French annexation of the European Netherlands in 1810 is not automatically propagated to already occupied Dutch islands.
completeness: Major established administrations, substantial occupations, treaty cessions and independence episodes are included within the stated island scope. Minute raids, every abandoned outpost, every administrative regrouping and all internal regimes are not exhaustive. Some early and disputed sequences remain editorial approximations, explicitly flagged at event level.
sourcePolicy: Government, treaty, library, museum and scholarly material is preferred. World Statesmen supplies much of the detailed colonial chronology and is a secondary compilation, not independent archival proof. Contradictions are resolved where local scholarship is stronger and otherwise exposed. A source link establishes provenance; it is not a claim that every event has two independent confirmations.
